page.title: Four million ants in your browser
page.description: Two anthills where every ant and queen is a tinyactors actor, up to four million of them, running in your browser on WebAssembly.

hero.headline: Four million actors in a browser tab.
hero.lede: Every ant and queen is a statechart, run by tinyactors in this page's Workers. Raise the colony to four million ants, or shorten their rests until the tab falls behind.

section.heading: Watch them.
section.p: An ant decides only when something happens: it leaves, finds food, comes home, meets an enemy. Between decisions your GPU draws it walking, and tinyactors does no work for it.
A resting ant costs memory and no work, so the rest slider sets how many messages the hosts handle a second.
The charts under the field measure this tab. When the ants send more messages than the hosts answer, the pace chart drops below real time.

playground.description: Two anthills on a field. Each colony's workers fetch food for their queen, who lays eggs with it, and workers of the two colonies fight where they meet.

section.heading: An ant is a statechart.
section.p: An egg hatches, a larva grows, and a worker forages, carries food home and rests. Two fights kill it, and so do old age, after 6 to 14 trips, and your tap.

section.heading: So is a queen.
section.p: Workers bring her food. Once a second she lays an egg for every two pieces.

section.heading: The world is an I/O processor.
section.p: When an ant asks to forage, the world picks where it goes and when it will arrive. It tells the ant when it gets there.

section.heading: Two hosts, two cores.
section.p: Each colony is a host in a Worker of its own, so the colonies decide in parallel.
A frame moves the clock 50 milliseconds, tells the ants that arrived, and answers a message for the other colony.
An ant that arrives where an enemy arrived under half a second earlier may fight it.
